cross_run_memo_persistence.verdict: INFEASIBLE in the current sandbox; structural cause recorded
findings: sandbox 16MiB memory cap: base working set (memo 262144-entry table + fbt cache + search) is ~13-15MB, leaving <1MB headroom; a full dump of the 117k proven bounds is ~4.7MB and exceeds the cap in-run (write_file arguments are retained by the run)

high-value-only persistence (win>=5 or lose>=4, ~15k lines) is I/O-feasible but resumption is ineffective: the ~89k dropped shallow facts (win<=3, lose<=2) are re-proven from scratch every run and consume most of the node budget; loaded entries produced 0 root-level memo hits and the cap frontier did not observably advance

memo table at 91% occupancy (238k/262k) causes memoEntry probe failures: the table then holds duplicate keys (4,766 dump lines -> 1,796 unique). MS=1<<19 would need ~2MB more and does not fit the 16MiB cap
file_system read_file truncates at ~64KB per call; cross-run loaders must loop offset/next_offset (an initial loader silently read only 1,594 of 14,737 lines)
cross_run_memo_persistence.conclusion: completing mob-50 candidates needs either a bigger-memory runner (external compute lane), a fundamentally smaller proof (certificate-chunked per-universal-child facts), or a better search. Do not retry naive cross-run memo persistence in the sandbox
